newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil earns $5.25 bln from 1996 privatizations.
newsitem.headline: Brazil earns $5.25 bln from 1996 privatizations.

text.p: Brazilian federal and state-level privatizations raised $5.252 billion in 1996, the Finance Ministry said.
It also said $670 million in debt of publicly owned companies was transferred to their new owners upon being sold during the year.

The figures represent an improvement on 1995, when privatization revenues totalled $1.003 billion, and $625 million in debt was transfered, the ministry said in a year-end analysis of the privatization program.
In 1996, the federal government raised $4.009 billion through privatizations, with $3.008 billion being paid in cash and the remaining $1.001 billion paid in securitized debt paper.

Two companies accounted for $1.24 billion raised in state-level privatizations in 1996 -- the sale of Rio's power utility CERJ, and the sale of a 33 percent stake in Rio Grande do Sul's CRT telecommunications company.
The document reiterated the federal government's aim of raising $10 billion via privatizations in 1997, including from mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce and from power generator Furnas.
It said steps have already been taken to separate Furnas from its nuclear power generating assets, which will not be included in the comany's privatization.
Studies by private consultants advising on the model of privatization for the power sector as a whole should be finished by May, the document said.

The renting out of space at Brazilian ports has raised 604 million reais through 36 contracts since October 1995, and contracts worth another 315 million reais are in the process of being tendered out.

At the state level, 17 state governments have signed agreements with the National Development Bank (BNDES) to privatize their companies, and 13 have been given the go-ahead to do so from their state legislatures.
Government officials said recently they expect state-level privatizations to raise $8.0 to $10 billion in 1997, with at least $5.0 billion earmarked for reducing debt.
